method: Read 323–375 in sequence; distinguish visual/ASR uncertainty from teachable language. Bodily vocabulary is receptive, with no instructions for abusive acts or treatment advice.
phrases: tossed onto a sheet
thrown onto a large piece of cloth, here apparently a bedsheet
被抛到一块布单上（这里看来指床单）
In the novel, the clothes were tossed onto a sheet on the floor.
小说里，衣服被扔到地板上的一块布单上。
Toss is throw; onto marks movement to a surface. A sheet is cloth in this scene, not a sheet of paper. Blindfolded and tossed share the passive I was in the quoted account.
flinging me up and down
throwing or moving me forcefully upward and downward repeatedly
把我用力上下抛动
In the story, the giant shouted, 'Stop flinging me up and down!'
故事里，巨人大喊：“别再把我上下抛来抛去了！”
Fling is a forceful throw. Me identifies the affected person; the participial phrase describes the repeated movement rather than a voluntary jump. No exact gesture or method is reconstructed.
slathered
spread a thick or generous layer of something over a surface
厚厚地涂抹；大量抹上
She slathered butter on the toast.
她在吐司上涂了厚厚的黄油。
Slather something on/over something; the generous amount distinguishes it from a light smear. Source describes alleged nonconsensual contact; the food example is an unrelated teaching illustration.
fistfuls
amounts that can be held in a closed hand
一把把；满把的量
He scattered fistfuls of seeds over the soil.
他把一把把种子撒在土上。
Fist + -ful names an approximate handful-sized quantity, not a punch. The plural means repeated amounts, not a precise measurement.
genitals
the external sexual organs
外生殖器
The textbook uses the neutral anatomical term genitals.
教科书使用了“外生殖器”这一中性的解剖学用语。
Plural anatomical noun, more formal than junk in paragraph 350. The source explicitly alleges unwanted contact; naming the body part does not supply consent.
oatmeal
a food made from oats, often cooked into a porridge
燕麦食品；这里指燕麦粥
I had oatmeal and fruit for breakfast.
我早餐吃了燕麦粥和水果。
American food sense; cold describes its temperature in the source. Mung is the speaker's name for the described mixture, not a claim that it contains mung beans or a standardized food name.
Smeared
spread over a surface, often unevenly
涂抹；抹得到处都是
Paint was smeared across the table.
油漆被抹得桌上到处都是。
Source is a passive fragment continuing the previous mixture description. Smeared is physical here, not the figurative reputational attack in smear someone's name.
consent to anyone touching him
agree to anyone making physical contact with him
同意任何人触碰他
He did not consent to anyone touching him during the demonstration.
他没有同意任何人在演示中触碰他。
Consent to + noun/-ing; to is a preposition, not an infinitive marker here. The source explicitly negates consent, and or inflicting continues the scope of that negation.
a half gallon
half of the volume called a gallon
半加仑（一种容量计量）
We bought a half gallon of milk.
我们买了半加仑牛奶。
An American volume expression; not half a bottle of unspecified size. The amount in the account is not a recommendation for treating pain or injury.
junk
an informal, sometimes crude term for male genitals in this context
男性生殖器（粗俗口语，此处不是垃圾）
The dialogue uses junk as slang for a man's genitals.
这段对话用 junk 这个俚语指男性生殖器。
Common everyday junk means unwanted stuff; here my spicy junk refers to the affected body area. Wash off names removal, not an endorsed medical treatment.
infamous
well known for something bad
臭名昭著的；因坏事出名的
The road is infamous for its traffic jams.
这条路因经常堵车而出名。
Unlike famous, carries a negative evaluation. The source's now is relative to the narration; this vocabulary note does not independently establish reputation or correct the Kai-Fi spelling.
great Fratsby
a fraternity-themed wordplay on the title The Great Gatsby
把《了不起的盖茨比》与 frat（兄弟会）结合的派对名称双关
The invitation called it a Great Fratsby party, a pun on The Great Gatsby.
邀请函把它称为“Great Fratsby”派对，借《了不起的盖茨比》的书名玩了个双关。
Frat is informal for fraternity; Fratsby is a coined name, not a normal adjective or a general idiom. The title allusion does not establish the actual party's decorations or activities.
segments: Sleep deprived and exhaustion are separate conditions; alleges/quote attribute the account. The two newly taught movement phrases cover passive throwing onto cloth and repeated forceful motion, without converting the account into a demonstrated technique.

Tossing him up is now lexically supported through toss/fling. Like this refers to an unseen gesture: the PDF does not show its exact motion or extent. Retain the visual-source gap even though the broad action is understood.

The surrounding unwanted-contact account suggests a euphemistic/ASR interpretation of essayed, but the verb cannot be silently replaced in a quote. First time marks absence of a prior experience; audio verification of the sensitive verb remains pending.

Waistband locates the shorts' upper edge; slather and fistfuls distinguish spreading and quantity. Mung is locally named and defined in 348, not assumed to mean beans. The unwanted bodily contact remains the quoted person's allegation, with no instructions added.

The existing composition connector plus the new oatmeal sense cover the remaining gap. Hot sauce is spicy sauce, cold is temperature, and mung is this account's name for the listed mixture. The lesson uses unrelated food and presentation examples, not an abuse recipe.

Passive smear continues the mixture account, followed by explicitly absent consent to contact or pain. Consent to + -ing and bodily terminology are now supported. Screamed bloody murder is already taught as loud distress, not a literal homicide claim.

Volume expression and the genital slang sense are now explicit. Was given is passive and to wash off states the narrated purpose, not verified treatment effectiveness; spicy refers to the irritating material described previously.

Negative reputation meaning is now taught; initiated connects to completed entry into the fraternity. Kai-Fi conflicts with other spellings in the transcript, and a teaching gloss cannot authenticate the proper name. Keep the exact PDF text and the unresolved name flag.

Read with the party name in 357 and planning reference in 363. Made posters for parties is clear, but like the houses does not yield a secure clause; do not invent a verb, location or transcription repair.

The coined fraternity/title pun now has explicit cultural support and a teaching example. Great belongs to the allusion, not merely the speaker rating the party; no unmentioned party theme details are invented.
